blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
How decisions really get made in a British organisation is rarely what the org chart suggests. The meeting is usually where decisions are confirmed, not where they are made. The real work happens in smaller rooms, in private conversations, in one-to-ones with the people who will sign off.

If you wanted something approved last week, you should have started talking to the key people the week before. Ambushing in the big meeting rarely works — it makes the decision-maker feel cornered, which pushes them into a cautious 'no'.

The trick is to build quiet agreement before the formal vote. Talk to the CFO about the numbers. Talk to operations about the risks. Turn up with the room already half-convinced. Once you see this rhythm, British decisions become much easier to win.

items.q: According to the text, what usually happens in the formal meeting?
options: The decision is confirmed rather than made
The decision is made for the first time
items.why: "The meeting is usually where decisions are confirmed, not where they are made."

items.q: Where does the text say the real work happens?
options: In the boardroom during the vote
In written reports to the CFO
In smaller rooms and private conversations
items.why: "The real work happens in smaller rooms, in private conversations, in one-to-ones."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: You should speak to key people before the meeting.
Quiet agreement is built one conversation at a time.
Presenting a surprise proposal in the big meeting is the best way to win approval.
A cornered decision-maker tends to say no.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que emboscar na reunião raramente funciona — o oposto de 'melhor forma de aprovar'.

items.q: The phrase "Turn up with the room already half-convinced" suggests that…
options: persuasion should happen before the meeting, not during it
the room should be kept undecided until the vote
the meeting itself should do most of the persuading
only half the people need to attend
items.why: Inferência: se a sala já chega meio convencida, o convencimento aconteceu antes — nas conversas prévias.

items.q: Why does ambushing push a decision-maker toward 'no'?
options: Because the numbers are usually wrong
Because the org chart forbids it
Because they feel cornered and become cautious
Because the meeting runs out of time
items.why: "it makes the decision-maker feel cornered, which pushes them into a cautious 'no'."

blocks.instruction: Ouça James orientando um novo diretor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so your budget goes to the committee on Thursday, and I can already tell you how this will go if you walk in cold. You'll present your slides, someone will ask a question you haven't cleared, and the chair will say, 'Let's take this offline.' That's a polite no.

Here's what I want you to do instead. Over the next few days, see the CFO on her own. Walk her through the numbers before she ever sees them on a screen. If she pushes back, you fix it privately — not in front of eleven people. Then go to operations and ask them what could go wrong. Don't defend the plan; just listen. When they raise a risk, thank them and build it in.

By Thursday, the CFO already knows the figures, operations feel heard, and two other heads owe you a favour from last quarter. The meeting isn't where you win. It's where you collect. You'll table the proposal, three people will nod, and it's done in four minutes.

If you'd done it this way last time, that project would have been approved in one sitting.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say will happen if the director "walks in cold"?
options: The chair will politely defer it with 'Let's take this offline'
The committee will cancel the meeting
The CFO will present the numbers for him
The proposal will be approved immediately
items.why: "the chair will say, 'Let's take this offline.' That's a polite no."

items.q: What does James advise doing with the CFO?
options: Send her the slides the morning of the meeting
Walk her through the numbers privately before the meeting
Let her hear the figures for the first time in the room
items.why: "see the CFO on her own. Walk her through the numbers before she ever sees them on a screen."

items.q: How should the director react when operations raise a risk?
options: Thank them and build it into the plan
items.why: "When they raise a risk, thank them and build it in."

items.q: What does James mean by "The meeting isn't where you win. It's where you collect"?
options: You should collect signatures during the meeting
You collect feedback to redo the plan later
The meeting is just a formality once the groundwork is done
The real debate happens in the meeting
items.why: Inferência: o convencimento já ocorreu antes; a reunião só ratifica o que foi construído.

items.q: What can we infer from James's final remark about the earlier project?
options: The director skipped the groundwork last time and it cost him
The CFO blocked the project deliberately
The project was never worth approving
The director followed this approach last time
items.why: Inferência (terceiro condicional): 'If you'd done it this way last time…' implica que da vez anterior ele não fez, e por isso falhou.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The org chart puts her three levels below the board, but everyone knows she really runs the place." An org chart is…
options: a diagram of who reports to whom
items.why: Org chart = organograma: o diagrama das linhas de reporte.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Nothing moves until the CFO gives her ___ on the spend."
items.why: Sign-off = aprovação/aval final, o que libera o gasto.

items.q: "Springing the proposal on him without warning felt like an ambush." An ambush is…
options: a sudden, unexpected attack or move
items.why: Ambush = emboscada: algo lançado de surpresa, sem aviso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With three tough questions in a row, she felt completely ___ and refused to commit."
items.why: Cornered = encurralado(a): sem saída, o que a leva a recuar.

items.q: "They reached a quiet agreement over coffee, long before the formal vote." A quiet agreement is…
items.why: Quiet agreement = acordo silencioso: consenso informal construído nos bastidores.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se prepara uma aprovação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "When operations pushed back on the timeline, he listened instead of arguing." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's take this offline and revisit it next week," the chair said. This usually means…
options: move the discussion to another platform
politely defer the matter out of the meeting
items.why: Take this offline = tirar o assunto da reunião para tratar depois — muitas vezes um 'não' educado.

items.q: "He agreed to help but never followed through." He…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Winning over two more heads before Thursday will really move the needle." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.
